knowledge:
- key_parameters:
  - object / dataset / target.pathway: A numeric matrix of gene expression where rows correspond to genes and columns correspond to samples.
  - group / group.label: A vector of factor or numeric labels (e.g., 1 and 2) indicating the experimental condition of each sample.
  - test: A character string in TestGeneSets specifying the test function to run (e.g., "GSNCAtest", "WWtest", "KStest").
  - min.size / max.size: Numeric thresholds in TestGeneSets to filter gene sets by the number of genes they contain.
  - max.skip: An integer in GSNCAtest specifying the maximum allowed skipped permutations when a permutation results in a gene with zero standard deviation.
- alternatives:
  - Competitive GSA approaches: These compare a gene set against its complement (all other genes). They can be biased by genomic coverage, data filtering, or the proportion of up/down-regulated genes. Self-contained methods in GSAR are preferred because they directly compare the gene set's expression between two phenotypes without complement bias.
- when_to_use:
  - Use GSAR when you want to perform self-contained gene set analysis to test specific biological hypotheses beyond simple differential expression, such as changes in pathway variance (scale) or pathway coexpression (net correlation structure).
  - Use it when you want to identify "hub genes" within a pathway and visualize how the pathway's correlation network topology changes between two conditions using Minimum Spanning Trees (MST2).
- pitfalls:
  - Zero standard deviation: In RNA-seq data, unexpressed genes may have zero or near-zero counts across samples, resulting in zero standard deviation. This causes errors in correlation-based tests like GSNCAtest. Genes with standard deviations below 1e-3 must be filtered out before running GSNCAtest.
  - RNA-seq variance-mean dependency: Because variance is a function of the mean in RNA-seq count data, applying variance-based tests (e.g., RKStest, RMDtest, RADtest, RCVMtest, AggrFtest) to RNA-seq data is highly sensitive to the normalization method used.
  - Matrix orientation: The findMST2 function requires a matrix with rows as genes and columns as samples. If your dataset has samples as rows, it must be transposed first.

workflows.name: microarray_gsa
workflows.intent: Perform self-contained gene set analysis on microarray expression data to test for differences in distribution, mean, variance, or correlation structure, and visualize the network.
input: p53DataSet (normalized microarray expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
c2.pathways (list of gene sets containing gene symbols)
workflows.stages:
1. Extract the expression matrix for the target pathway.
2. Define the sample group labels.
3. Run individual statistical tests (WWtest for distribution, KStest/MDtest/ADtest/CVMtest for mean, RKStest/RMDtest/RADtest/RCVMtest/AggrFtest for variance, and GSNCAtest for net correlation).
4. Plot the MST2 correlation network for the pathway under both conditions to identify hub genes.
5. Run GSA on multiple gene sets sequentially using the TestGeneSets wrapper.
workflows.code:
target.pathway <- p53DataSet[c2.pathways[["LU_TUMOR_VASCULATURE_UP"]],]
group.label <- c(rep(1,17), rep(2,33))
WW_pvalue <- WWtest(target.pathway, group.label)
KS_pvalue <- KStest(target.pathway, group.label)
MD_pvalue <- MDtest(target.pathway, group.label)
AD_pvalue <- ADtest(target.pathway, group.label)
CVM_pvalue <- CVMtest(target.pathway, group.label)
RKS_pvalue <- RKStest(target.pathway, group.label)
RMD_pvalue <- RMDtest(target.pathway, group.label)
RAD_pvalue <- RADtest(target.pathway, group.label)
RCVM_pvalue <- RCVMtest(target.pathway, group.label)
F_pvalue <- AggrFtest(target.pathway, group.label)
GSNCA_pvalue <- GSNCAtest(target.pathway, group.label)
plotMST2.pathway(object=p53DataSet[c2.pathways[[path.index]],], group=c(rep(1,17), rep(2,33)), name="LU_TUMOR_VASCULATURE_UP", legend.size=1.2, leg.x=-1.2, leg.y=2, label.size=1, label.dist=0.8, cor.method="pearson")
results <- TestGeneSets(object=p53DataSet, group=group.label, geneSets=c2.pathways[1:3], min.size=10, max.size=100, test="GSNCAtest")

workflows.name: rnaseq_gsa
workflows.intent: Perform self-contained gene set analysis on RNA-seq count data, handling normalization and filtering of zero-variance genes.
input: PickrellDataSet (RNA-seq count matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
XYgenes (vector of genes in the target pathway)
workflows.stages:
1. Filter out low-expressed genes using count-per-million (CPM) thresholds.
2. Normalize counts using RPKM and log2-transform the data.
3. Extract the target pathway expression matrix.
4. Filter out genes with zero or tiny standard deviation (< 1e-3) in either group to avoid errors in correlation-based tests like GSNCA.
5. Run statistical tests (WWtest, KStest) on the normalized, filtered pathway matrix.
workflows.code:
cpm.matrix <- cpm(PickrellDataSet)
cpm.means <- rowMeans(cpm.matrix)
cpm.filter <- which(cpm.means > 0.1)
PickrellDataSet <- PickrellDataSet[cpm.filter,]
genes.length <- genes.length[cpm.filter]
rpkm.set <- rpkm(PickrellDataSet, genes.length)
rpkm.set <- log2(1 + rpkm.set)
XYpathway <- rpkm.set[XYgenes,]
group.label.pickrell <- (gender == "male") + 1
WW_pvalue <- WWtest(XYpathway, group.label.pickrell)
KS_pvalue <- KStest(XYpathway, group.label.pickrell)
tiny.sd.XY.female <- which(apply(XYpathway[, group.label.pickrell == 1], 1, "sd") < 1e-3)
tiny.sd.XY.male <- which(apply(XYpathway[, group.label.pickrell == 2], 1, "sd") < 1e-3)
if(length(tiny.sd.XY.male) > 0) XYpathway <- XYpathway[-tiny.sd.XY.male,]
if(length(tiny.sd.XY.female) > 0) XYpathway <- XYpathway[-tiny.sd.XY.female,]
